To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a phase field model that can be used for the simulation of hydraulic fracturing and microcracking in highly heterogeneous saturated porous media with interfacially damaged inclusions.

(i) interfacial damage is a crucial factor in the hydraulic fracturing process; (ii) fluid flow through interfacial cracks is a key factor in the hydraulic fracture propagation; (iii) the proposed numerical model allows for a fully coupled description of fluid flow in both the matrix and interfacial crack network.
we have developed a novel phase field model for hydraulic fracturing or crack propagation in heterogeneous saturated porous materials that can be applied to regular voxel-based geometries.

the development of a phase field framework for the modeling of hydro-mechanical cracking in heterogeneous fluid-saturated media.
a phase field model for hydraulic fracturing or hydraulic cracking in highly heterogeneous fluid saturated porous media.
the modeling of hydraulic fracture in heterogeneous fluid-saturated media.
